manifest.name: Website Payment
manifest.description: Bridge module that adds multi-website support for payment providers plus the public /donation pages.

models._description: Account Payment (donation flag, related to tx)

views.qweb_templates: donation_pay payment page + s_donation / s_supported_payment_methods snippets

behavioral_notes.observation: donation_pay is the public storefront entry: it forces is_donation=True, defaults currency to the company currency and amount to 25.0, seeds a customAmount=freeAmount donation_options blob, and for a public (anonymous) visitor assigns the public partner and mints an access_token via payment_utils.generate_access_token(partner, amount, currency) before delegating to the inherited payment_pay to render the form. donation_transaction is the JSON-RPC that actually builds the payment.transaction from the visitor-typed free amount: it enforces amount >= minimum_amount, requires name/email/country for anonymous donors (attached as partner_name/email/country_id on the tx), calls _create_transaction (engine), sets tx.is_donation, then RECOMPUTES the access_token against the final amount (because the donor can change the amount on the page) and updates the landing route, finally calling _send_donation_email as an internal recipient notification. The free-amount-to-transaction binding and access-token re-issue are pure controller logic invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: PaymentPortal.payment_pay / payment_method overrides (controllers/payment.py) — website-aware provider scoping
behavioral_notes.observation: controllers/payment.py is a thin override of account_payment.PaymentPortal that re-dispatches the generic 'pay' page and the manage-payment-methods portal page (/my/payment_method) passing website_id=request.website.id. This propagates into payment.provider._get_compatible_providers (models/payment_provider.py), which filters the provider set to those whose website_id is unset OR equals the current website, logging the rest into the availability report as 'incompatible_website'. The result: the public pay page and the portal payment-method manager only expose providers published/scoped to the website the visitor is on — multi-website provider isolation that no field metadata reveals. PortalAccount._invoice_get_page_view_values is likewise made website-aware.

Public readonly endpoint feeding the 'supported payment methods' website snippet: it computes the website's compatible providers with_user(website.user_id).sudo() (so editors preview exactly what customers see, scoped to website.company_id rather than the visitor's company), then selects brand payment.methods (e.g. Amex under Card) plus brandless primary methods (e.g. PayPal), returning [{name, image_url}] where image_url is a cacheable website image URL. It sets Cache-Control to no-cache for internal users but 'public, max-age=604800, stale-while-revalidate=86400' (7 days) for public/portal — a client-cache strategy entirely in controller code.

On settlement, _post_process (override of the engine hook) filters the done donation transactions and, per tx, sends a donor confirmation email and logs a chatter message on tx.payment_id (the account.payment) listing company/partner/name/country/email of the donation. _send_donation_email renders website_payment.donation_mail_body (encapsulated in mail.mail_notification_light) in the recipient's language and sends via mail.mail; it is invoked twice in the flow — once at transaction creation as an internal notification to donation_recipient_email, and again on done as the donor confirmation. This couples the donation payment to mail + account.payment chatter, invisible to metadata.

The donation pay page is driven on the client by a patch of the engine's PaymentForm: it wires the free-amount radio/'other amount' inputs into paymentContext.amount, validates the minimum on submitForm, and in _prepareTransactionRouteParams injects partner_id, currency_id, reference_prefix, partner_details {name,email,country_id}, donation_comment and donation_recipient_email into the JSON-RPC to /donation/transaction. A separate DonationForm public interaction handles snippet UX (amount selection, comment toggle, min-amount warnings). This is the static-asset half of the free-amount donation flow.

it_architecture.application: website_payment (Website Payment bridge — exposes the payment engine on the public website / portal)
logical_data_erm: payment.transaction -> res.partner (donor; anonymous donors use website public partner)
information_flows: depends: website, account_payment, portal (no new models; 4 inherit-only extensions)
scoping: website_id -> payment.provider._get_compatible_providers -> provider set filtered to current website on pay / manage-method pages
side-effect: donation done -> _post_process -> _send_donation_email (mail.mail) + chatter log on account.payment
snippet: /website_payment/snippet/supported_payment_methods -> website-scoped payment.method brands -> cached JSON to s_supported_payment_methods snippet
frontend_components: PaymentForm.prototype patch (donation amount binding + transaction route params)
donation_pay QWeb payment page; s_donation + s_supported_payment_methods website snippets

external_integrations.pattern: No direct outbound HTTP in this bridge: actual acquirer communication is delegated to the inherited payment engine (payment.provider._send_api_request) and per-acquirer override modules. This module only adds website-scoping and the donation storefront on top of that engine.
external_integrations.note: uses_api_keys=true is inherited from the payment stack; website_payment itself opens no new external endpoints (gap #7 lives in the base payment + provider modules).

donation minimum-amount enforcement (server-side amount >= minimum_amount; client-side warnings)

metrics: donation transaction volume / amounts (payment.transaction where is_donation, via payment engine pivot/graph)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (online payment collection / donations via the public website)
classification.rationale: This is a storefront/portal mediation bridge: it implements no payment processing itself (no new models, only inherit-only extensions and public controllers) — it EXPOSES the underlying payment value-network on the public website. Stabell & Fjeldstad value_model = 'network' (mediating technology): like the base payment engine it interconnects a paying party (website visitor / donor) and the merchant/acquirer, here by provisioning that mediation through the public web channel (network promotion = the donation + supported-methods snippets that advertise the means to transact; service provisioning = the /donation/transaction that binds a free amount to a payment.transaction; infrastructure operation = the website-scoped provider selection routing the visitor to the right acquirer). We diverge from the base payment record on activity_class: payment.metamodel set it 'support' (back-office engine, category Hidden). Here the module is a CUSTOMER-FACING website surface (category Website/Website) whose function is online collection of money / donations from the public — a revenue-facing, market-and-sell activity — so activity_class = 'primary'. APQC 3.0 (Market and Sell) is chosen over 9.0 (Manage Financial Resources, where the back-office engine sits) precisely because the value here is collecting payment from a customer at the point of sale/solicitation on the website, not internal treasury processing; a 9.5 'process payments' reading would understate that this is the public collection front end. activity_class=primary + value_model=network captures both that it is revenue-facing and that its internal logic is mediation, not transformation.

standard_capabilities: public /donation/pay page with prefilled + free-amount options
donation transaction creation from a visitor free amount with minimum-amount enforcement
donor + recipient confirmation emails on settlement, chatter log on the payment
per-website payment provider scoping on the pay page and the portal manage-methods page
drag-and-drop website snippets: Donation (s_donation) and Supported Payment Methods (s_supported_payment_methods)
anonymous donation via website public partner (tokenization suppressed)
typical_fits: non-profit / fundraising site collecting one-off donations of arbitrary amount
multi-website group routing each site's checkout to its own acquirer set
showing accepted card brands / wallets as a trust snippet on a landing page
logged-in portal customers managing saved cards scoped to the current website
common_gaps: no live acquirer ships here — a payment_<provider> module is still required to actually charge
recurring / pledged donations (this module is one-off free-amount only)
donation tax receipts / gift-aid style fiscal documents (beyond the confirmation email)
bespoke donation analytics dashboards (only the generic payment.transaction reporting exists)
custom landing-route / post-settlement document creation beyond the donation email + chatter
drive_hints: curl -i 'http://localhost:8069/website_payment/snippet/supported_payment_methods' (public; returns JSON PM list + Cache-Control)
curl GET /donation/pay on a published website to render the donation form

open_questions: Which downstream/sibling modules (website_sale, website_event) reuse /donation or the website-scoped provider filtering, and how donations reconcile in accounting.
Real-world donation volumes and how often anonymous-vs-logged-in donation paths are used (no runtime row counts captured).
Exact acquirer endpoints/auth remain in per-provider override modules, not in this bridge.
